title: Classic Carrot Cake
description: A hearty old-fashioned carrot cake — dense, moist, deeply spiced, and sturdy enough to slice for days without apology.

ingredients.notes: softened at room temperature for 2 hours
added a little at a time

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 150°C. Grease a 28 cm round cake tin with butter or margarine. Line the base and sides with baking paper and grease the paper as well.

In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine eggs, sugar, self-raising flour, vanilla extract, oil, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. Mix with the whisk attachment until the mixture is fairly thick and stiff.
Transfer mixture to a large stainless steel bowl.
Add finely grated carrots, sultanas, and chopped walnuts. Mix in with a wooden spoon until evenly combined. Do not drain the carrots — their natural moisture keeps the cake tender.
Pour mixture into the prepared tin and smooth the surface.
Place a deep tray of water on the lower oven rack to create moisture and prevent the bottom from burning.
Bake for 2½–3 hours, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.
For the frosting: allow cream cheese to soften at room temperature for at least 2 hours. Beat with an electric mixer until smooth, scraping down the bottom and sides of the bowl.
Add icing sugar gradually, about ¼ cup at a time, mixing until the mixture becomes smooth and paste-like.
Add lemon juice a little at a time — do not add too much. Mix until combined.
Add vanilla extract to taste and mix to finish.
Spread frosting generously over the cooled cake.

notes.title: Slow Bake
notes.content: The low temperature and long bake produce a dense, moist crumb that improves over the next day. The water tray creates steam to prevent the surface from drying out and stops the bottom from burning.

notes.title: Carrot Moisture
notes.content: Do not squeeze or drain the grated carrots. Their natural moisture is essential to the cake's texture — it releases slowly during the long bake, keeping the crumb tender.

notes.title: Wooden Spoon Mixing
notes.content: Mix the carrots, sultanas, and walnuts in by hand with a wooden spoon. The batter is thick and stiff — folding gently by hand prevents overworking the gluten.

notes.title: Frosting Consistency
notes.content: Add lemon juice slowly — too much will make the frosting runny. The mixture should go like paste before adding vanilla. Soften the cream cheese for a full 2 hours for the smoothest result.

notes.title: Serving Tip
notes.content: Keeps well for several days refrigerated. Bring to room temperature before serving. The flavour deepens overnight.
